<!--
An advice sheet is the short public document that carries the catch advice to managers. It
is heavily standardised: the section order below is the one ICES uses and IMR follows, and
readers navigate by it. Do not reorder or rename the sections.

Every number in an advice sheet is inline R, without exception. The sheet is regenerated
each year against a new assessment, it is quoted directly by managers and press, and a
stale number is a public error.
-->

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "report_helpers.R"))

ensure_packages("flextable", "officer", "icesAdvice")

# Advice-sheet tables carry real subscripts, merged group rows, and footnotes, and Word clips
# a table wider than the text column rather than reflowing it. Set the house defaults once,
# and size figures to the column for Word output.
flextable::set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family = "Calibri", font.size = 9, table.layout = "fixed",
  border.color = "black", big.mark = " ", decimal.mark = ".", padding = 2
)
if (identical(knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to"), "docx")) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "6.3in")
}
```

```{r release-values}
#| include: false
# ── VALUES THAT CHANGE AT RELEASE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# These cannot be derived from the assessment. They are the annual edit, kept in one place.
# Leave them as visible placeholders until the advisory body supplies them: a plausible-looking
# DOI that resolves to nothing is worse than an obvious blank.
publication_line <- "Published DD Month YYYY"
advice_doi       <- "[DOI TO BE ASSIGNED]"
download_url     <- "[DOWNLOAD URL TO BE ASSIGNED]"
```

```{r advice-values}
#| include: false
#| eval: false
# Every value quoted below, derived once from the assessment output: the advised catch, the
# stock status relative to each reference point, the change from last year's advice, and the
# catch-scenario table. Read a SAVED ASSESSMENT SUMMARY here, not the fitted model object —
# that keeps the sheet fast and guarantees it quotes the same numbers as the assessment report.
#
# ay      <- params$advice_year
# advice  <- <look the advice-rule row up BY NAME, never by row position>
# change  <- 100 * (advice - params$prev_advice) / params$prev_advice
#
# Derive the status sentence rather than writing it, so the prose cannot contradict the table:
#
# b_status <- dplyr::case_when(
#   bbmsy < blim ~ "below B~lim~",
#   bbmsy < btrigger ~ "below MSY B~trigger~ but above B~lim~",
#   .default = "above MSY B~trigger~"
# )
#
# Captions that carry a year are built here as strings and referenced with `!expr`:
# cap_catch_scenarios <- paste0("Annual catch scenarios for ", ay, ". Catches in tonnes.")
```

<!--
Where the assessment behind this sheet is EXPLORATORY — a supplement to an official assessment
rather than the official one — open with a callout saying so and naming the official model, and
treat it as load-bearing. An exploratory sheet mistaken for official advice is the worst
failure this document type has, and a tidying pass is exactly how such a callout gets dropped.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Exploratory assessment — not official advice
...
:::
-->

# Catch scenarios

<!--
The table is GROUPED: an "Advice basis" row, the advice-rule scenario, an "Other scenarios"
row, then the rest. Group rows are merged across the table, bold, and shaded. The percentage
columns are the change in biomass and the change from the previous advice; where there was no
previous advice that column is a dash with a footnote saying why, never a zero, which reads as
"no change".

Reference points in a header or a cell need real subscripts — flextable does not read markdown
inside a cell, so compose them:

    flextable::compose(ft, part = "header", j = f_col,
      value = flextable::as_paragraph("F", flextable::as_sub("MSY")))

See the academic-advice-sheet skill for the house style and the page-fitting helper.
-->

# Basis of the assessment

## Software and reproducibility

The assessment was run in `r R.version.string` [@rcoreteam]. This sheet was compiled with Quarto [@quarto] and rendered by knitr [@knitr], and is reproducible from the assessment output.

This document and the associated analyses were created with researcher-supervised generative AI (<!-- MODEL -->). The authors specified and checked the assessment, and reviewed, edited, and approved all AI-assisted content, for which they take full responsibility.

      "2024" = list(advice = "MSY approach", advised_catch = 4200, tac = 4000),
      "2025" = list(advice = "MSY approach", advised_catch = 3900, tac = 3900)
    )

When the assessment year advances, EXTEND the list. Never pad, recycle, or shorten the year
